transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-08-02 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48 mins
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Sofia Ruiz (Redwood Solutions), Rina Patel (Aperture Head of Infra), Tom Becker (Cloud Architect), Amira Nelson (Security), Priya Shah (ML Eng)

Summary: quick alignment on POC success criteria, network topology choices (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), regional residency constraints, egress limitations and benchmark plan. Agreed to a two-week benchmarking window mid-August; Redwood to deliver test scripts and docs.

00:00:03 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, ill kick off, quick agenda — scope, success criteria, network options, bench plan and next steps
00:00:14 Rina: thanks maya, quick context — we need all inference traffic to remain in eu-west-1 or on prem in frankfurt for PHI, and egress strictly controlled, so peering vs privatelink matters for us
00:00:33 Liam: got it. for residency we support both peering and privatelink; tradeoffs are throughput and egress NATing, privatelink gives endpoint isolation but can add cost and extra hops sometimes
00:00:50 Tom: and our security wants to avoid shared routing tables crossing other accounts — so prefer endpoint that doesn't require broad route pushes
00:01:05 Amira: yes also we have an HSM/KMS requirement — keys must be customer-managed, and audit logs must be forwarded to our splunk instance in eu-west-1
00:01:20 Sofia: quick note, for private deploy we can integrate with KMS and forward audit events, we'll include the runbook for log forwarding
00:01:35 Priya: on workload sizing — current prod is approx 120 QPS peak for text-gen, avg payload 320 tokens, max 2k tokens when long-form notes, embedding traffic ~8 QPS separate pipeline
00:01:50 Maya: that's helpful — our bench will test 3 traffic shapes: low-latency live path (50 qps, 8-512 tokens), peak throughput (150 qps steady for 30m, 320 avg tokens) and sporadic long-tail (burst to 300 qps for 5m and 2k tokens). is that representative?
00:02:12 Priya: yes mostly, though bursts might be a bit higher during batch runs, say 350 qps peak for 2–3 mins
00:02:25 Liam: ok we’ll adjust scripts to include a burst window. target SLOs to validate?
00:02:33 Rina: P95 latency under 200ms for short prompts, p95 under 800ms for long prompts, and error rate under 0.1% sustained. Cost per token target is also a hard internal metric but we can treat as secondary for POC
00:02:49 Maya: noted — success criteria: 1) residency verified (no egress outside eu-west-1), 2) latency SLOs as rina said, 3) throughput targets with <0.1% errors, 4) integration with our KMS and audit pipeline
00:03:08 Tom: curious — how does privatelink egress look for outbound to S3 for logs? we prefer logs never traverse internet egress to public S3 endpoints
00:03:22 Sofia: we support VPC endpoints to S3 in the same region, and the private deployment can be configured to use VPC endpoint policies so logs stay private; we'll document the exact route tables and proxy config
00:03:38 Amira: about certs — we'll need mutual TLS for internal calls, can the Redwood agents support mTLS to our sidecar?
00:03:48 Liam: yes we have an mTLS option in private-deploy; small note: cert rotation interacts with KMS keys but it's supported — we'll capture the steps
00:04:00 Maya: switching to topology tradeoffs. quick bullets: VPC peering — simpler, lower latency, but requires route-table updates and could expand blast radius. PrivateLink — smaller blast radius, RBAC per endpoint, but sometimes adds a NAT hop and per-GB charges. any other pros/cons?
00:04:23 Tom: latency is main concern, but operational overhead of peering across our multiple accounts is non-trivial
00:04:34 Priya: also we have a future plan for regional lock — want to ensure we can pin to eu-west-1 and failover to eu-central if needed, but no egress to other continents
00:04:48 Maya: we can set routing and model pins; Redwood supports model variants in region and automatic fallback to a compatible quantized variant inside the region — will document failover policy
00:05:05 Rina: benchmarks — what exactly will you measure?
00:05:10 Liam: latency P50/P95/P99, throughput sustained qps, token cost, error types and root cause (timeouts, oom, rate-limit), and residency verification via traceroute/firewall logs and packet capture samples we can anonymize
00:05:30 Tom: will you simulate KV cache hits? our workload often has repeating prefixes so cached KV is important for costs
00:05:38 Liam: yes we'll include a warm-cache run and cold-cache run; note transcription might read KV cache as K-V cash but — we'll make sure to label
00:05:48 Priya: bench duration?
00:05:52 Maya: propose 3 day warmup ramp, then 2 weeks of tests including multiple 4–8 hour sustained windows and burst tests, but you said earlier two-week window starting aug 16 — does that still work?
00:06:08 Rina: aug 16 starts are ok, but decrease the initial warmup to 24 hours, we have limited permission windows for cross-account peering changes
00:06:18 Lily: (speaker glitch) — sorry, we lost priya for a sec —
00:06:25 Priya: i'm here, yes 24 hr warmup is doable
00:06:30 Amira: security review — please share SOC2 report, ISO certs, pen test summary, and our legal wants to see the data handling addendum
00:06:41 Maya: noted, we'll drop a folder in the shared drive with those artifacts and redact sensitive items; I'll include a KMS integration note and HSM support doc
00:06:54 Tom: on fail open vs fail closed — if our KMS is unavailable do we want Redwood to fail the requests or to fail open to keep serving? we prefer fail closed for PHI
00:07:06 Liam: by default private deploy can be configured to fail closed; we'll include runbook for handling KMS outage and recommended timeout values
00:07:18 Rina: also curious about monitoring — we need token-level cost breakdowns per route and tracing hooks; is that in the standard console or add-on?
00:07:29 Sofia: token-level cost is available in console as an add-on; in a POC we can enable a temporary extended retention so you can validate cost models, and provide the breakdowns as csvs too
00:07:42 Priya: for the bench scripts, we need variability in prompt distribution — can you accept a custom prompt set so we can compare generation quality regressions?
00:07:52 Liam: absolutely — we'll run your prompt suite for regen checks and include quality metrics and a small eval harness; we'll need a non-PII subset or anonymized prompts for public artifacts
00:08:07 Maya: ok next, timeline recap: Aug 5 — runbook & pricing, Aug 6 — customer traffic & IAM, Aug 10 — bench script, Aug 16 — benchmark start for 2 weeks, post-benchmark review week of Aug 30. everyone aligned?
00:08:22 Rina: yes aligned
00:08:26 Amira: one more item — egress control for third-party models, we do not want any model or telemetry hitting US-based endpoints; ensure all images and code pulls are region-local
00:08:39 Liam: we can pin images to eu-region registries for the POC; will note to remove any auto-updates during the test window to avoid unexpected outbound calls
00:08:53 Tom: about cost—if we choose privatelink and RBC style per-endpoint pricing, what's the ballpark uplift?
00:09:02 Maya: rough thumb: privatelink could add 10–30% infra costs depending on traffic egress; we'll give a more precise delta in the runbook and a scenario table with your traffic numbers
00:09:15 Priya: ok good. any blockers?
00:09:18 Rina: only approvals for cross-account peering and legal signoff for DPA — those are internal and we can try to push them in this window
00:09:26 Maya: great. final quick q from my side: are we ok to run network tests that will require transient route updates (peering) during business hours?
00:09:38 Tom: we'll schedule peering updates during our maintenance window; prefer weekend but can do early morning weekday if needed
00:09:48 Sofia: i'll include a change window recommendation in the runbook and a checklist for rollback
00:09:55 Maya: excellent. i'll send materials and a calendar invite for the bench kickoff. thanks everyone
00:10:02 (meeting continues with some technical clarifications and side discussions about IAM roles and endpoint policies — notes truncated)

Action item recap: Maya to send docs (runbook, pricing), Tom to provide traces and IAM snippets, Liam to prepare bench tools.
